\section{Proof of the main theorem}\label{sec:assembly}

Fix $f$ as in \cref{thm:main}. The finiteness and positivity of $C_f$ are \cref{prop:poly}(0). Let $x\ge2$ and $y\ge1$ be real with $Y=f(y)\le x$, and fix $\eps>0$.

\emph{Range of the moduli.} The hypothesis $f'(t)\ge1$ for all \emph{real} $t\ge1$ makes $f$ increasing on $[1,\infty)$. Hence every integer $1\le k\le y$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:moduli-range}
2\le f(k)\le f(y)=Y\le x .
\end{equation}
So \cref{prop:single} applies to $q=f(k)$ with the same $x$, for every $k\le y$, with a constant independent of $k$. By~\eqref{eq:Vf}, $V_f(x,y)=\sum_{1\le k\le y}f'(k)V(x;f(k))$, and $f'(k)>0$.

\emph{Elementary inequalities.} Write $f(t)=\sum_{i\le d}\alpha_it^i$ and $\gamma_0=\sum_i|\alpha_i|$. For $y\ge1$, $Y\le\gamma_0y^d$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:y-Y}
y^{-1/2}\le\gamma_0^{1/(2d)}\,Y^{-1/(2d)}.
\end{equation}
Since $Y\le x$, we have $Y^\eps\le x^\eps$ and $1+\log Y\le1+\log x\le C'(\eps)x^\eps$. With \cref{prop:poly}(b),(c) this gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sums}
\sum_{k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}\le c_8(f)C'(\eps)\,x^{\eps},\qquad\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c_8(f)\,Y .
\end{equation}

\subsection{Part (ii)}

Apply \cref{prop:single}(i) with $\eps/2$ to each $q=f(k)$, multiply by $f'(k)$ and sum over $1\le k\le y$:
\[
\Bigl|V_f(x,y)-\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\MT(x;f(k))\Bigr|\le c_7(\tfrac\eps2)\Bigl(x^{5/3+\eps/2}\sum_{k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\Bigr).
\]
By~\eqref{eq:sums} with $\eps/2$, the right-hand side is at most
\[
c_7(\tfrac\eps2)\,c_8(f)\bigl(C'(\tfrac\eps2)\,x^{5/3+\eps}+x^{1/2}Y\bigr),
\]
which is part~(ii).

\subsection{Part (i)}

Apply \cref{prop:single}(ii) with $\eps/3$ to each $q=f(k)$ and use $f'(k)\sqrt{f(k)}=F(k)$:
\[
\Bigl|V_f(x,y)-\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))\Bigr|\le c_7(\tfrac\eps3)\,(T_1+T_2+T_3),
\]
where the three sums are bounded as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item $T_1=x^{1/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)f(k)^{2/3+\eps/3}\le x^{1/3}Y^{2/3+\eps/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c_8(f)\,x^{1/3+\eps/3}Y^{5/3}$, by $f(k)\le Y\le x$ and~\eqref{eq:sums}.
\item $T_2=x^{5/3+\eps/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)/f(k)\le c_8(f)C'(\tfrac\eps3)\,x^{5/3+2\eps/3}$, by~\eqref{eq:sums} with $\eps/3$.
\item $T_3=\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c_8(f)\,x^{1/2}Y\le c_8(f)\,x^{1/2}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}$, because $Y\ge2$ and $\frac12-\frac1{2d}\ge0$.
\end{itemize}
For the main term, \cref{prop:poly}(a) with $\eps/3$ and~\eqref{eq:y-Y} give
\begin{align*}
\Bigl|\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\Bigr|&\le c_8(f,\tfrac\eps3)\gamma_0^{1/(2d)}\,x^{1/2}Y^{3/2+\eps/3-1/(2d)}\\
&\le c_8(f,\tfrac\eps3)\gamma_0^{1/(2d)}\,x^{1/2+\eps/3}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}.
\end{align*}
By the triangle inequality,
\[
\bigl|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\bigr|\le c(f,\eps)\Bigl(x^{1/3+\eps}Y^{5/3}+x^{5/3+\eps}+x^{1/2+\eps}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}\Bigr),
\]
with $c(f,\eps)=c_7(\tfrac\eps3)c_8(f)\bigl(2+C'(\tfrac\eps3)\bigr)+c_8(f,\tfrac\eps3)\gamma_0^{1/(2d)}$. This is part~(i).

\subsection{Part (iii)}

Fix $\delta\in(0,1/9)$. The interval $[x^{7/9+\delta},x^{1-\delta}]$ is nonempty for $x>1$ exactly because $7/9+\delta<1-\delta$. Assume $x^{7/9+\delta}\le Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, put $\eta=\min(\delta/12,1/(6d))$, and apply~(i) with $\eps=\min(\delta/12,1/(9d))$. We divide each error term by $x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item $x^{-1/6+\eps}Y^{1/6}\le x^{-1/6+\eps+(1-\delta)/6}=x^{\eps-\delta/6}\le x^{-\delta/12}\le x^{-\eta}$, using $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ and $\eps\le\delta/12$;
\item $x^{7/6+\eps}Y^{-3/2}\le x^{7/6+\eps-\frac32(7/9+\delta)}=x^{\eps-3\delta/2}\le x^{-\delta/12}\le x^{-\eta}$, using $Y\ge x^{7/9+\delta}$ and $\frac32\cdot\frac79=\frac76$;
\item $x^{\eps}Y^{-1/(2d)}\le x^{\eps-7/(18d)}\le x^{1/(9d)-7/(18d)}=x^{-5/(18d)}\le x^{-1/(6d)}\le x^{-\eta}$, using $Y\ge x^{7/9}$ and $\eps\le1/(9d)$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence $|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}|\le3c(f,\eps)\,x^{-\eta}x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$, where $\eps$ depends only on $\delta$ and $d$. As $0<C_f<\infty$, this is $V_f(x,y)=C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\bigl(1+O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\eta})\bigr)$. \qed

\begin{remark}
The exponent $\eta$ is conservative. The third ratio is in fact at most $x^{-5/(18d)}$, and the second at most $x^{-17\delta/12}$. We keep the exponent as it was stated in the archived proof.
\end{remark}
# Proof of P9 (assembly)

No external literature is used. The proof uses only P7, P8 and elementary estimates. No numerical checks were run, since none are needed.

Throughout, $f$ is fixed. "Constant" means a constant depending only on $f$, and on $\varepsilon$ or $\delta$ where indicated. Let $x\ge2$, $y\ge1$ and $Y=f(y)\le x$.

## 0. Preliminaries

**(P-a) Range of moduli.** Since $f'(t)\ge1>0$ for $t\ge1$, $f$ is increasing on $[1,\infty)$. So every integer $k$ with $1\le k\le y$ has $2\le f(k)\le f(y)=Y\le x$. Hence P7 applies to $q=f(k)$ for every $k\le y$, with the same $x$. Also $Y\ge f(1)\ge2$.

**(P-b) Decomposition.** By definition $V_f(x,y)=\sum_{1\le k\le y}f'(k)\,V(x;f(k))$, where $V(x;q)=\sum_{l=1}^qE(x;q,l)^2$.

**(P-c) Size of $y$ in terms of $Y$.** Write $f(t)=\sum_{i\le d}a_it^i$. For $y\ge1$,
$$Y=f(y)\le\Big(\sum_i|a_i|\Big)y^d=:c_1y^d .$$
So $y\ge(Y/c_1)^{1/d}$, and therefore
$$y^{-1/2}\le c_1^{1/(2d)}\,Y^{-1/(2d)}.\tag{0.1}$$

**(P-d) Logarithm.** Since $Y\le x$, we have $1+\log Y\le1+\log x\le c(\varepsilon)x^{\varepsilon}$. Likewise $Y^{\varepsilon}\le x^{\varepsilon}$.

**Consequences of P8(b),(c).**
$$\sum_{k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}\le c(f)(1+\log Y)\le c(f,\varepsilon)x^{\varepsilon},\qquad \sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c(f)Y.\tag{0.2}$$

## 1. Proof of (ii)

Apply P7(i) with $\varepsilon$ to each $q=f(k)$, $k\le y$. This is legitimate by (P-a). We get
$$|V(x;f(k))-MT(x;f(k))|\le c(\varepsilon)\Big(\frac{x^{5/3+\varepsilon}}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\Big).$$
Multiply by $f'(k)>0$, sum over the $\lfloor y\rfloor$ integers $1\le k\le y$, and use the triangle inequality and (P-b):
$$\Big|V_f(x,y)-\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)MT(x;f(k))\Big|\le c(\varepsilon)\Big(x^{5/3+\varepsilon}\sum_{k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\Big).$$
By (0.2), the right side is at most
$$c(\varepsilon)\big(c(f,\varepsilon')x^{5/3+\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}+c(f)\sqrt x\,Y\big)$$
for any $\varepsilon'>0$. Choosing $\varepsilon=\varepsilon'=\varepsilon_0/2$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is the $\varepsilon$ in the claim, gives
$$\le c(f,\varepsilon_0)\big(x^{5/3+\varepsilon_0}+x^{1/2}Y\big).$$
This is (ii). $\square$

## 2. Proof of (i)

Apply P7(ii) with $\varepsilon/3$ for each $q=f(k)$, $k\le y$ (legitimate by (P-a)):
$$\big|V(x;f(k))-h(f(k))\sqrt{x f(k)}\big|\le c(\varepsilon)\Big(x^{1/3}f(k)^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}+\frac{x^{5/3+\varepsilon/3}}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\Big).$$
Multiply by $f'(k)$ and sum over $1\le k\le y$. Note that $f'(k)\sqrt{f(k)}=F(k)$. Then
$$\Big|V_f(x,y)-\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))\Big|\le c(\varepsilon)\,(T_1+T_2+T_3),$$
where each $T_i$ is bounded as follows.

* **$T_1$.** Since $f(k)\le Y$, we have $f(k)^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}\le Y^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}$. So, by (0.2) and (P-d),
$$T_1=x^{1/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)f(k)^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}\le x^{1/3}Y^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}\cdot c(f)Y\le c(f)\,x^{1/3+\varepsilon/3}Y^{5/3}.$$
* **$T_2$.** By (0.2), $T_2=x^{5/3+\varepsilon/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)/f(k)\le c(f,\varepsilon)x^{5/3+2\varepsilon/3}\le c(f,\varepsilon)x^{5/3+\varepsilon}$.
* **$T_3$.** By (0.2), $T_3=\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c(f)\sqrt xY$. Since $Y\ge2$ and $d\ge1$, $Y^{1/2-1/(2d)}\ge1$, so $Y\le Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}$. Hence $T_3\le c(f)\,x^{1/2}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}$.

For the main term, P8(a) with $\varepsilon/3$ gives
$$\Big|\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))-C_fY^{3/2}\Big|\le c(f,\varepsilon)Y^{3/2+\varepsilon/3}y^{-1/2}.$$
By (0.1) the right side is at most $c(f,\varepsilon)Y^{3/2-1/(2d)+\varepsilon/3}$. Multiplying by $\sqrt x$ and using $Y^{\varepsilon/3}\le x^{\varepsilon/3}$ gives
$$\Big|\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\Big|\le c(f,\varepsilon)\,x^{1/2+\varepsilon/3}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}.$$

Combine the bounds via the triangle inequality: the first error is at most $c(\varepsilon)(T_1+T_2+T_3)$, and this last bound controls the main-term error. This gives
$$|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}|\le c(f,\varepsilon)\big(x^{1/3+\varepsilon}Y^{5/3}+x^{5/3+\varepsilon}+x^{1/2+\varepsilon}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}\big),$$
which is (i). $\square$

## 3. The consequence

Fix $\delta\in(0,1/9)$ and assume $x^{7/9+\delta}\le Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ (with $y\ge1$, $x\ge2$). Put $\eta=\min(\delta/12,1/(6d))$ and take $\varepsilon=\min(\delta/12,\,1/(9d))$ in (i). Divide the error in (i) by $x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$ and bound each of the three ratios.

1. $\dfrac{x^{1/3+\varepsilon}Y^{5/3}}{x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}=x^{-1/6+\varepsilon}Y^{1/6}\le x^{-1/6+\varepsilon+(1-\delta)/6}=x^{-\delta/6+\varepsilon}\le x^{-\delta/12}\le x^{-\eta}$.
 Here we used $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ and $\varepsilon\le\delta/12$.

2. $\dfrac{x^{5/3+\varepsilon}}{x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}=x^{7/6+\varepsilon}Y^{-3/2}\le x^{7/6+\varepsilon-\frac32(7/9+\delta)}=x^{-3\delta/2+\varepsilon}\le x^{-\delta/12}\le x^{-\eta}$.
 Here we used $Y\ge x^{7/9+\delta}$, $\tfrac32\cdot\tfrac79=\tfrac76$ and $\varepsilon\le\delta/12$.

3. $\dfrac{x^{1/2+\varepsilon}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}}{x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}=x^{\varepsilon}Y^{-1/(2d)}\le x^{\varepsilon-\frac{7}{18d}-\frac{\delta}{2d}}\le x^{\frac1{9d}-\frac7{18d}}=x^{-\frac5{18d}}\le x^{-\frac1{6d}}\le x^{-\eta}$.
 Here we used $Y\ge x^{7/9+\delta}\ge x^{7/9}$, $\varepsilon\le1/(9d)$ and $\tfrac5{18}\ge\tfrac16=\tfrac3{18}$.

Summing the three ratios, (i) gives
$$|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}|\le 3c(f,\delta)\,x^{-\eta}\,x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}.$$
By P8(0), $0<C_f<\infty$. So $3c(f,\delta)x^{-\eta}x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}=C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\cdot O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\eta})$, and
$$V_f(x,y)=C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\big(1+O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\eta})\big).\qquad\blacksquare$$

Remark: $\delta<1/9$ makes the range $x^{7/9+\delta}\le Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ non-empty, since $7/9+\delta<1-\delta$ exactly when $\delta<1/9$.

Hence $|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}|\le3c(f,\eps)\,x^{-\eta}x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$, where $\eps$ depends only on $\delta$ and $d$. As $0<C_f<\infty$, this is $V_f(x,y)=C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\bigl(1+O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\eta})\bigr)$. \qed

\begin{remark}
The exponent $\eta$ is conservative. The third ratio is in fact at most $x^{-5/(18d)}$, and the second at most $x^{-17\delta/12}$. We keep the exponent as it was stated in the archived proof.
\end{remark}
# Proof of P9 (assembly)

No external literature is used. The proof uses only P7, P8 and elementary estimates. No numerical checks were run, since none are needed.

Throughout, $f$ is fixed. "Constant" means a constant depending only on $f$, and on $\varepsilon$ or $\delta$ where indicated. Let $x\ge2$, $y\ge1$ and $Y=f(y)\le x$.

## 0. Preliminaries

**(P-a) Range of moduli.** Since $f'(t)\ge1>0$ for $t\ge1$, $f$ is increasing on $[1,\infty)$. So every integer $k$ with $1\le k\le y$ has $2\le f(k)\le f(y)=Y\le x$. Hence P7 applies to $q=f(k)$ for every $k\le y$, with the same $x$. Also $Y\ge f(1)\ge2$.

**(P-b) Decomposition.** By definition $V_f(x,y)=\sum_{1\le k\le y}f'(k)\,V(x;f(k))$, where $V(x;q)=\sum_{l=1}^qE(x;q,l)^2$.

**(P-c) Size of $y$ in terms of $Y$.** Write $f(t)=\sum_{i\le d}a_it^i$. For $y\ge1$,
$$Y=f(y)\le\Big(\sum_i|a_i|\Big)y^d=:c_1y^d .$$
So $y\ge(Y/c_1)^{1/d}$, and therefore
$$y^{-1/2}\le c_1^{1/(2d)}\,Y^{-1/(2d)}.\tag{0.1}$$

**(P-d) Logarithm.** Since $Y\le x$, we have $1+\log Y\le1+\log x\le c(\varepsilon)x^{\varepsilon}$. Likewise $Y^{\varepsilon}\le x^{\varepsilon}$.

**Consequences of P8(b),(c).**
$$\sum_{k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}\le c(f)(1+\log Y)\le c(f,\varepsilon)x^{\varepsilon},\qquad \sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c(f)Y.\tag{0.2}$$

## 1. Proof of (ii)

Apply P7(i) with $\varepsilon$ to each $q=f(k)$, $k\le y$. This is legitimate by (P-a). We get
$$|V(x;f(k))-MT(x;f(k))|\le c(\varepsilon)\Big(\frac{x^{5/3+\varepsilon}}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\Big).$$
Multiply by $f'(k)>0$, sum over the $\lfloor y\rfloor$ integers $1\le k\le y$, and use the triangle inequality and (P-b):
$$\Big|V_f(x,y)-\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)MT(x;f(k))\Big|\le c(\varepsilon)\Big(x^{5/3+\varepsilon}\sum_{k\le y}\frac{f'(k)}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\Big).$$
By (0.2), the right side is at most
$$c(\varepsilon)\big(c(f,\varepsilon')x^{5/3+\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}+c(f)\sqrt x\,Y\big)$$
for any $\varepsilon'>0$. Choosing $\varepsilon=\varepsilon'=\varepsilon_0/2$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is the $\varepsilon$ in the claim, gives
$$\le c(f,\varepsilon_0)\big(x^{5/3+\varepsilon_0}+x^{1/2}Y\big).$$
This is (ii). $\square$

## 2. Proof of (i)

Apply P7(ii) with $\varepsilon/3$ for each $q=f(k)$, $k\le y$ (legitimate by (P-a)):
$$\big|V(x;f(k))-h(f(k))\sqrt{x f(k)}\big|\le c(\varepsilon)\Big(x^{1/3}f(k)^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}+\frac{x^{5/3+\varepsilon/3}}{f(k)}+\sqrt x\Big).$$
Multiply by $f'(k)$ and sum over $1\le k\le y$. Note that $f'(k)\sqrt{f(k)}=F(k)$. Then
$$\Big|V_f(x,y)-\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))\Big|\le c(\varepsilon)\,(T_1+T_2+T_3),$$
where each $T_i$ is bounded as follows.

* **$T_1$.** Since $f(k)\le Y$, we have $f(k)^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}\le Y^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}$. So, by (0.2) and (P-d),
$$T_1=x^{1/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)f(k)^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}\le x^{1/3}Y^{2/3+\varepsilon/3}\cdot c(f)Y\le c(f)\,x^{1/3+\varepsilon/3}Y^{5/3}.$$
* **$T_2$.** By (0.2), $T_2=x^{5/3+\varepsilon/3}\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)/f(k)\le c(f,\varepsilon)x^{5/3+2\varepsilon/3}\le c(f,\varepsilon)x^{5/3+\varepsilon}$.
* **$T_3$.** By (0.2), $T_3=\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}f'(k)\le c(f)\sqrt xY$. Since $Y\ge2$ and $d\ge1$, $Y^{1/2-1/(2d)}\ge1$, so $Y\le Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}$. Hence $T_3\le c(f)\,x^{1/2}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}$.

For the main term, P8(a) with $\varepsilon/3$ gives
$$\Big|\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))-C_fY^{3/2}\Big|\le c(f,\varepsilon)Y^{3/2+\varepsilon/3}y^{-1/2}.$$
By (0.1) the right side is at most $c(f,\varepsilon)Y^{3/2-1/(2d)+\varepsilon/3}$. Multiplying by $\sqrt x$ and using $Y^{\varepsilon/3}\le x^{\varepsilon/3}$ gives
$$\Big|\sqrt x\sum_{k\le y}F(k)h(f(k))-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\Big|\le c(f,\varepsilon)\,x^{1/2+\varepsilon/3}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}.$$

Combine the bounds via the triangle inequality: the first error is at most $c(\varepsilon)(T_1+T_2+T_3)$, and this last bound controls the main-term error. This gives
$$|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}|\le c(f,\varepsilon)\big(x^{1/3+\varepsilon}Y^{5/3}+x^{5/3+\varepsilon}+x^{1/2+\varepsilon}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}\big),$$
which is (i). $\square$

## 3. The consequence

Fix $\delta\in(0,1/9)$ and assume $x^{7/9+\delta}\le Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ (with $y\ge1$, $x\ge2$). Put $\eta=\min(\delta/12,1/(6d))$ and take $\varepsilon=\min(\delta/12,\,1/(9d))$ in (i). Divide the error in (i) by $x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}$ and bound each of the three ratios.

1. $\dfrac{x^{1/3+\varepsilon}Y^{5/3}}{x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}=x^{-1/6+\varepsilon}Y^{1/6}\le x^{-1/6+\varepsilon+(1-\delta)/6}=x^{-\delta/6+\varepsilon}\le x^{-\delta/12}\le x^{-\eta}$.
 Here we used $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ and $\varepsilon\le\delta/12$.

2. $\dfrac{x^{5/3+\varepsilon}}{x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}=x^{7/6+\varepsilon}Y^{-3/2}\le x^{7/6+\varepsilon-\frac32(7/9+\delta)}=x^{-3\delta/2+\varepsilon}\le x^{-\delta/12}\le x^{-\eta}$.
 Here we used $Y\ge x^{7/9+\delta}$, $\tfrac32\cdot\tfrac79=\tfrac76$ and $\varepsilon\le\delta/12$.

3. $\dfrac{x^{1/2+\varepsilon}Y^{3/2-1/(2d)}}{x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}}=x^{\varepsilon}Y^{-1/(2d)}\le x^{\varepsilon-\frac{7}{18d}-\frac{\delta}{2d}}\le x^{\frac1{9d}-\frac7{18d}}=x^{-\frac5{18d}}\le x^{-\frac1{6d}}\le x^{-\eta}$.
 Here we used $Y\ge x^{7/9+\delta}\ge x^{7/9}$, $\varepsilon\le1/(9d)$ and $\tfrac5{18}\ge\tfrac16=\tfrac3{18}$.

Summing the three ratios, (i) gives
$$|V_f(x,y)-C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}|\le 3c(f,\delta)\,x^{-\eta}\,x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}.$$
By P8(0), $0<C_f<\infty$. So $3c(f,\delta)x^{-\eta}x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}=C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\cdot O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\eta})$, and
$$V_f(x,y)=C_fx^{1/2}Y^{3/2}\big(1+O_{f,\delta}(x^{-\eta})\big).\qquad\blacksquare$$

Remark: $\delta<1/9$ makes the range $x^{7/9+\delta}\le Y\le x^{1-\delta}$ non-empty, since $7/9+\delta<1-\delta$ exactly when $\delta<1/9$.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Regenerate every number in the manuscript's numerical tables and plots.
3	
4	Invoke from the workspace root:
5	
6	    python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
7	
8	What it does (details in manuscript/README.md):
9	
10	1. Copies the accepted snapshot's ``compute.py`` and ``counts.cpp`` from
11	   ``source/numerics/snapshot`` into a scratch work directory (after checking
12	   their SHA-256 against ``source/numerics/accepted.json``) and runs
13	   ``compute.py`` there unchanged.  That script compiles ``counts.cpp`` with
14	   clang++, re-runs its validations, recomputes V_f(x, y) on the full grid
15	   x = 2.5e5, ..., 2.56e8, and redoes the empirical fits.  The archived
16	   executable is not used.
17	2. Compares the regenerated ``results.json`` with the archived one.
18	3. Computes, with code in this file, the quantities of the theorem that are
19	   not part of the snapshot: the constant C_f (Euler product over p <= 1e7,
20	   with a rigorous bound for the omitted primes), Vaughan's constant c_2,
21	   the sums  sum_k f'(k) MT(x; f(k))  and  sum_k F(k) h(f(k))  at selected rows,
22	   and a self-test of the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2).
23	4. Writes LaTeX table fragments and PGFPlots data files to
24	   ``manuscript/generated/`` and the index ``manuscript/reproduction.json``.
25	
26	No value is copied from proof prose or from the archived results; the
27	archived ``results.json`` is read only for the agreement check in step 2.
28	"""
29	import argparse
30	import hashlib
31	import itertools
32	import json
33	import math
34	import pathlib
35	import shutil
36	import subprocess
37	import sys
38	import time
39	from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_FLOOR
40	
41	import numpy as np
42	import mpmath as mp
43	import sympy
44	
45	HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
46	WS = HERE.parent
47	SNAP = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'snapshot'
48	ACCEPTED = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'accepted.json'
49	GEN = HERE / 'generated'
50	DEFAULT_WORK = WS / 'scratch' / 'reproduce-work'
51	MARKER = '.reproduce-work'
52	
53	NAMES = ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2', '2k+1']
54	TEXNAME = {'k^2+1': '$k^2+1$', 'k^3+2': '$k^3+2$', '2k+1': '$2k+1$', 't': '$t$ (formal)'}
55	POLY = {'k^2+1': (lambda k: k * k + 1, lambda k: 2 * k, 2),
56	        'k^3+2': (lambda k: k ** 3 + 2, lambda k: 3 * k * k, 3),
57	        '2k+1': (lambda k: 2 * k + 1, lambda k: 2, 1),
58	        't': (lambda k: k, lambda k: 1, 1)}
59	RATIOS = [.01, .02, .05, .1, .2, .4, .7, 1.]
60	PRIME_CUTOFFS = [10 ** 3, 10 ** 4, 10 ** 5, 10 ** 6, 10 ** 7]
61	# Rows of the exact-shape comparison (Table 5).  The linear polynomial has
62	# about x/2 moduli, so it is restricted to the two smallest sizes.
63	SHAPE_XS = {'k^2+1': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
64	            'k^3+2': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
65	            '2k+1': [250000, 1000000]}
66	
67	mp.mp.dps = 80
68	I_CONST = -4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)          # I = -4 zeta(-1/2)
69	SIX_PI2 = 6 / mp.pi ** 2
70	
71	
72	def sha256(path):
73	    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
74	
75	
76	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	# 1. Snapshot re-run
78	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
79	
80	def run_snapshot(work, reuse):
81	    accepted = json.loads(ACCEPTED.read_text())['artifacts']
82	    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
83	        if sha256(SNAP / name) != accepted[name]:
84	            raise RuntimeError(f'{name} does not match the accepted snapshot hash')
85	    elapsed = None
86	    if not (reuse and (work / 'results.json').exists()):
87	        if work.exists():
88	            # Only ever delete a directory that this script created itself.
89	            if any(work.iterdir()) and not (work / MARKER).exists():
90	                raise RuntimeError(f'{work} is not empty and was not created by reproduce.py; '
91	                                   'choose another --work directory')
92	            shutil.rmtree(work)
93	        work.mkdir(parents=True)
94	        (work / MARKER).write_text('scratch directory of manuscript/reproduce.py; safe to delete\n')
95	        for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
96	            shutil.copy2(SNAP / name, work / name)
97	        t0 = time.monotonic()
98	        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(work / 'compute.py')], cwd=work, check=True)
99	        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
100	    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
101	        if sha256(work / name) != accepted[name]:
102	            raise RuntimeError(f'work copy of {name} differs from the snapshot')
103	    results = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
104	    return results, elapsed
105	
106	
107	def all_rows(res, name):
108	    p = res['polynomials'][name]
109	    return p['rows'] + p['diagnostic_rows']
110	
111	
112	def compare_with_archive(new):
113	    old = json.loads((SNAP / 'results.json').read_text())
114	    out = {}
115	    for name in NAMES:
116	        o = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(old, name)}
117	        n = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(new, name)}
118	        if set(o) != set(n):
119	            raise RuntimeError(f'row sets differ for {name}')
120	        exact = all(o[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted'] == n[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted']
121	                    and o[k]['y'] == n[k]['y'] for k in o)
122	        dv = max(abs(Decimal(o[k]['V_decimal']) / Decimal(n[k]['V_decimal']) - 1) for k in o)
123	        po, pn = old['polynomials'][name], new['polynomials'][name]
124	        ce_o, ce_n = po['constant_extrapolated'], pn['constant_extrapolated']
125	        out[name] = dict(rows=len(o), integer_counts_identical=exact,

138	def primes_upto(n):
139	    s = np.ones(n + 1, dtype=bool)
140	    s[:2] = False
141	    for p in range(2, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
142	        if s[p]:
143	            s[p * p::p] = False
144	    return np.nonzero(s)[0]

147	def powmod_vec(base, exp, mod):
148	    """Elementwise base**exp % mod for int64 arrays with mod < 3e9."""
149	    base = base % mod
150	    result = np.ones_like(mod)
151	    exp = exp.copy()
152	    while np.any(exp > 0):
153	        odd = (exp & 1) == 1
154	        result = np.where(odd, (result * base) % mod, result)
155	        base = (base * base) % mod
156	        exp >>= 1
157	    return result

160	def rho_formula(name, P):
161	    """(rho(p), rho(p^2)) for each prime in P, from the closed forms listed in
162	    Section 10.2.  They are checked against brute force by rho_bruteforce_check."""
163	    P = P.astype(np.int64)
164	    if name == 'k^2+1':
165	        r1 = np.where(P == 2, 1, np.where(P % 4 == 1, 2, 0))
166	        r2 = np.where(P == 2, 0, r1)
167	    elif name == 'k^3+2':
168	        cube = powmod_vec(np.full_like(P, -2), (P - 1) // 3, P) == 1
169	        r1 = np.where((P == 2) | (P == 3) | (P % 3 == 2), 1, np.where(cube, 3, 0))
170	        r2 = np.where((P == 2) | (P == 3), 0, r1)
171	    elif name == '2k+1':
172	        r1 = np.where(P == 2, 0, 1)
173	        r2 = r1.copy()
174	    elif name == 't':
175	        r1 = np.ones_like(P)
176	        r2 = np.ones_like(P)
177	    return r1.astype(np.float64), r2.astype(np.float64)

180	def rho_bruteforce_check(name, bound=1000):
181	    f = POLY[name][0]
182	    P = primes_upto(bound)
183	    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
184	    for i, p in enumerate(P):
185	        p = int(p)
186	        for m, expect in [(p, r1[i]), (p * p, r2[i])]:
187	            a = np.arange(m, dtype=np.int64)
188	            val = f(a) % m if name != 'k^3+2' else ((a * a % m) * a + 2) % m
189	            if int(np.count_nonzero(val == 0)) != int(expect):
190	                raise RuntimeError(f'rho mismatch for {name} at {m}')
191	    return len(P)

194	def local_factors(p):
195	    p = p.astype(np.float64)
196	    a_m1 = -3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3                                  # a_p - 1
197	    ba = -1 / p + p ** -1.5 + p ** -2 - p ** -2.5                     # b_p - a_p
198	    cb = -p ** -1.5 * (1 - p ** -0.5) * (1 - 1 / p)                  # c_p - b_p
199	    return a_m1, ba, cb

202	def euler_constant(name, P):
203	    """Partial values (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p and a rigorous interval for
204	    the full product (tail bound of Section 10.2)."""
205	    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
206	    xp, zp = r1 / P, r2 / (P.astype(np.float64) ** 2)
207	    a_m1, ba, cb = local_factors(P)
208	    s_m1 = a_m1 + ba * xp + cb * zp                                   # sigma_p - 1
209	    if np.any(1 + s_m1 <= 0):
210	        raise RuntimeError('nonpositive local factor')
211	    logs = np.log1p(s_m1)
212	    pref = 2 * float(I_CONST) / 3
213	    partial = {}
214	    for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS:
215	        partial[N] = pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N]))
216	    d = POLY[name][2]
217	    K = 3 + 2 * d
218	    N = PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]
219	    # |log prod_{p>N} sigma_p| <= K/(1-K/N^2) * sum_{p>N} p^-2, and every prime
220	    # p > N >= 30 lies in one of 8 classes mod 30, each contributing at most
221	    # N^-2 + 1/(30N).
222	    tail = K / (1 - K / N ** 2) * 8 * (1 / N ** 2 + 1 / (30 * N))
223	    val = partial[N]
224	    return dict(partial=partial, value=val, lower=val * math.exp(-tail),
225	                upper=val * math.exp(tail), tail_log_bound=tail, K=K)

228	def vaughan_c2(P):
229	    """c_2 = 8 C_1 (-zeta(-1/2)) / (3 zeta(2)^2), Vaughan (2005), (1.14)-(1.15)
230	    with k = 2; C_1 truncated to p <= N."""
231	    p = P.astype(np.float64)
232	    term = ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** 1.5 - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
233	    logs = np.log1p(term)
234	    pref = float(8 * (-mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / (3 * mp.zeta(2) ** 2))
235	    return {N: pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N])) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS}

259	def euler_float_check(name, N=10 ** 5, dps=40):
260	    """Recompute (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p with mpmath at dps digits, to
261	    gauge the floating-point rounding of euler_constant (not a certification)."""
262	    P = primes_upto(N)

265	        tot = mp.mpf(0)
266	        for p, a1, a2 in zip(P.tolist(), r1.tolist(), r2.tolist()):
267	            p = mp.mpf(p)
268	            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
269	            b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3
270	            c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
271	            xp, zp = mp.mpf(int(a1)) / p, mp.mpf(int(a2)) / p ** 2
272	            tot += mp.log(a * (1 - xp) + b * (xp - zp) + c * zp)
273	        return 2 * (-4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / 3 * mp.exp(tot)

290	def symbolic_local_identity():
291	    p = sympy.symbols('p', positive=True)
292	    r = sympy.sqrt(p)
293	    a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
294	    b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + r) / p ** 3
295	    c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
296	    sig = a * (1 - 1 / p) + b * (1 / p - 1 / p ** 2) + c / p ** 2
297	    C1p = 1 + ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** sympy.Rational(3, 2) - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
298	    checks = {
299	        'sigma_p(rho=1) == C_{1,p} (1-p^-2)^2': sympy.simplify(sig - C1p * (1 - p ** -2) ** 2) == 0,
300	        'a_p == (p-1)^2(p+2)/p^3': sympy.simplify(a - (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 2) / p ** 3) == 0,
301	        'b_p - a_p == -1/p + p^-3/2 + p^-2 - p^-5/2': sympy.simplify(b - a - (-1 / p + p ** sympy.Rational(-3, 2) + p ** -2 - p ** sympy.Rational(-5, 2))) == 0,

304	    }

310	def A0_mp():
311	    """A_0 = prod_p (1 - 2/p^2) to ~40 digits."""
312	    P0 = 1000
313	    small = [int(p) for p in primes_upto(P0)]
314	    head = mp.fsum(mp.log(1 - mp.mpf(2) / p ** 2) for p in small)
315	    tail = mp.mpf(0)
316	    for k in range(1, 30):
317	        pz = mp.primezeta(2 * k) - mp.fsum(mp.mpf(p) ** (-2 * k) for p in small)
318	        tail -= mp.mpf(2) ** k / k * pz
319	    return mp.exp(head + tail)

322	def Ah_mp():
323	    """A_h = prod_p (1 - 3/p^2 + 2/p^3) to ~40 digits."""
324	    P0 = 1000
325	    small = [int(p) for p in primes_upto(P0)]
326	    head = mp.fsum(mp.log(1 - mp.mpf(3) / p ** 2 + mp.mpf(2) / p ** 3) for p in small)
327	    tail = mp.mpf(0)
328	    for k in range(2, 30):
329	        ck = -(2 + mp.mpf(-2) ** k) / k
330	        pz = mp.primezeta(k) - mp.fsum(mp.mpf(p) ** (-k) for p in small)
331	        tail += ck * pz
332	    return mp.exp(head + tail)

339	class Arithmetic:
340	    """eta(t) for t <= tmax and the constants entering MT and h."""
341	    TSTAR = 64     # head of the eta-sums evaluated in 80-digit arithmetic
342	
343	    def __init__(self, tmax):
344	        tmax = max(tmax, self.TSTAR + 1)
345	        self.tmax = tmax
346	        eta = np.ones(tmax + 1)
347	        eta[0] = 0.
348	        for p in primes_upto(tmax):
349	            p = int(p)
350	            eta[p::p] /= (p * p - 2)
351	            eta[p * p::p * p] = 0.
352	        self.eta = eta
353	        self.t = np.arange(tmax + 1, dtype=np.float64)
354	        self.kappa = eta * self.t ** 2
355	        self.eta_t2 = np.divide(eta, self.t ** 2, out=np.zeros_like(eta), where=self.t > 0)
356	        self.A0mp = A0_mp()
357	        self.A0 = float(self.A0mp)
358	        self.Ahmp = Ah_mp()
359	        self.head_cache = {}
360	        self.eta_mp = [mp.mpf(0)] + [mp.mpf(1) for _ in range(self.TSTAR)]
361	        for t in range(1, self.TSTAR + 1):
362	            fac = sympy.factorint(t)
363	            if any(e > 1 for e in fac.values()):
364	                self.eta_mp[t] = mp.mpf(0)
365	            else:
366	                self.eta_mp[t] = mp.fprod(mp.mpf(1) / (p * p - 2) for p in fac)
367	
368	    def heads(self, qprimes, th):
369	        """80-digit A_0 * sum_{t<=th,(t,q)=1} eta(t) and eta(t)/t^2."""
370	        small = tuple(p for p in qprimes if p <= self.TSTAR)
371	        key = (small, th)
372	        if key not in self.head_cache:
373	            s2 = s4 = mp.mpf(0)
374	            for t in range(1, th + 1):
375	                if self.eta_mp[t] and all(t % p for p in small):
376	                    s2 += self.eta_mp[t]
377	                    s4 += self.eta_mp[t] / t ** 2
378	            self.head_cache[key] = (self.A0mp * s2, self.A0mp * s4)
379	        return self.head_cache[key]
380	
381	    def MT(self, x, q, fac):
382	        """MT(x; q) for integer x, q with q <= x; fac = factorisation of q.
383	
384	        Uses the factorisation t = t0 t1 t2 of the proof of Proposition 6.2:
385	        for t0 > sqrt(Z),
386	        B(Z/t0^2) = Z/t0^2 - Z^2/t0^4, and the complete eta-sums over t0 coprime
387	        to q are known in closed form, so the infinite t0-sum is evaluated
388	        exactly up to rounding."""
389	        S1 = [p for p, e in fac.items() if e == 1]
390	        S2 = [p for p, e in fac.items() if e >= 2]
391	        qprimes = list(fac)
392	        E2 = math.prod(1 + 1 / (p * p - 2) for p in S2)
393	        full2 = SIX_PI2 * mp.fprod(mp.mpf(p * p - 2) / (p * p - 1) for p in qprimes)
394	        full4 = SIX_PI2 ** 2 * mp.fprod(mp.mpf(p * p) * (p * p - 2) / (p * p - 1) ** 2 for p in qprimes)
395	        Tmax = math.isqrt(x // q)
396	        if Tmax > self.tmax:
397	            raise RuntimeError('tmax too small')
398	        ts = np.arange(1, Tmax + 1)
399	        cop = (self.eta[1:Tmax + 1] > 0) & (np.gcd(ts, q) == 1)
400	        total = 0.
401	        for r in range(len(S1) + 1):
402	            for sub in itertools.combinations(S1, r):
403	                t1 = math.prod(sub)
404	                eta1 = math.prod(1 / (p * p - 2) for p in sub)
405	                Z = x / (q * t1)
406	                T = math.isqrt(x // (q * t1))
407	                if T >= 1:
408	                    u = Z / self.t[1:T + 1] ** 2
409	                    fr = u - np.floor(u)
410	                    SB = float(np.sum((self.kappa[1:T + 1] * fr * (1 - fr))[cop[:T]]))
411	                else:
412	                    SB = 0.
413	                th = min(T, self.TSTAR)
414	                h2, h4 = self.heads(qprimes, th)
415	                br2, br4 = float(full2 - h2), float(full4 - h4)
416	                if T > self.TSTAR:
417	                    m = cop[self.TSTAR:T]
418	                    br2 -= self.A0 * float(np.sum(self.eta[self.TSTAR + 1:T + 1][m]))
419	                    br4 -= self.A0 * float(np.sum(self.eta_t2[self.TSTAR + 1:T + 1][m]))
420	                total += eta1 * t1 * (self.A0 * SB + Z * br2 - Z * Z * br4)
421	        return q * E2 * total
422	
423	    def h(self, fac):
424	        """h(q) = I prod_{p not | q} a_p prod_{p||q} b_p prod_{p^2|q} c_p."""
425	        val = self.Ahmp * I_CONST
426	        for p, e in fac.items():
427	            p = mp.mpf(p)
428	            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
429	            lam = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3 if e == 1 else (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
430	            val *= lam / a
431	        return float(val)

434	def factor_table(values):
435	    vmax = max(values)
436	    if vmax <= 2 * 10 ** 7:
437	        spf = np.zeros(vmax + 1, dtype=np.int32)
438	        for p in primes_upto(math.isqrt(vmax) + 1):
439	            p = int(p)
440	            blk = spf[p * p::p]
441	            blk[blk == 0] = p
442	        out = []
443	        for v in values:
444	            fac = {}
445	            while v > 1:
446	                p = int(spf[v]) or v
447	                while v % p == 0:
448	                    v //= p
449	                    fac[p] = fac.get(p, 0) + 1
450	            out.append(fac)
451	        return out
452	    return [{int(p): int(e) for p, e in sympy.factorint(v).items()} for v in values]

455	def identity_selftest(ar):
456	    """Check the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2) at x = 3000 for
457	    q <= 40, with every term computed by brute force except MT, which uses
458	    Arithmetic.MT.  Returns the largest relative discrepancy."""
459	    x = 3000
460	    sf = np.ones(x + 1, dtype=np.int64)
461	    sf[0] = 0
462	    for d in range(2, math.isqrt(x) + 1):
463	        sf[d * d::d * d] = 0
464	    c6 = float(SIX_PI2)
465	    Qx = int(sf.sum())
466	    worst = 0.
467	    for q in range(1, 41):
468	        fac = {int(p): int(e) for p, e in sympy.factorint(q).items()}
469	        g = np.empty(q)
470	        for l in range(q):
471	            v = c6 / q * math.prod(1 / (1 - p ** -2) for p in fac)
472	            for p, e in fac.items():
473	                if e == 1 and l % p == 0:
474	                    v *= 1 - 1 / p
475	                if e >= 2 and l % (p * p) == 0:
476	                    v = 0.
477	            g[l] = v
478	        n = np.arange(1, x + 1)
479	        counts = np.bincount(n % q, weights=sf[1:], minlength=q)
480	        E = counts - g * x
481	        V = float(np.sum(E ** 2))
482	        Dsum = 0.
483	        for hh in range(1, x // q + 1):
484	            m = hh * q
485	            C = int(np.sum(sf[1:x - m + 1] * sf[1 + m:x + 1]))
486	            A = ar.A0 * sum(ar.eta[t] for t in range(1, math.isqrt(m) + 1) if m % (t * t) == 0)
487	            Dsum += C - A * (x - m)
488	        rhs_wo_MT = 2 * Dsum + (Qx - c6 * x) - 2 * x * float(np.sum(g * E))
489	        mt = ar.MT(x, q, fac)
490	        worst = max(worst, abs(V - (mt + rhs_wo_MT)) / max(1., abs(V)))
491	    return worst

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regenerate every number in the manuscript's numerical tables and plots.

Invoke from the workspace root:

    python3 manuscript/reproduce.py

What it does (details in manuscript/README.md):

1. Copies the accepted snapshot's ``compute.py`` and ``counts.cpp`` from
   ``source/numerics/snapshot`` into a scratch work directory (after checking
   their SHA-256 against ``source/numerics/accepted.json``) and runs
   ``compute.py`` there unchanged.  That script compiles ``counts.cpp`` with
   clang++, re-runs its validations, recomputes V_f(x, y) on the full grid
   x = 2.5e5, ..., 2.56e8, and redoes the empirical fits.  The archived
   executable is not used.
2. Compares the regenerated ``results.json`` with the archived one.
3. Computes, with code in this file, the quantities of the theorem that are
   not part of the snapshot: the constant C_f (Euler product over p <= 1e7,
   with a rigorous bound for the omitted primes), Vaughan's constant c_2,
   the sums  sum_k f'(k) MT(x; f(k))  and  sum_k F(k) h(f(k))  at selected rows,
   and a self-test of the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2).
4. Writes LaTeX table fragments and PGFPlots data files to
   ``manuscript/generated/`` and the index ``manuscript/reproduction.json``.

No value is copied from proof prose or from the archived results; the
archived ``results.json`` is read only for the agreement check in step 2.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import math
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_FLOOR

import numpy as np
import mpmath as mp
import sympy

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WS = HERE.parent
SNAP = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'snapshot'
ACCEPTED = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'accepted.json'
GEN = HERE / 'generated'
DEFAULT_WORK = WS / 'scratch' / 'reproduce-work'
MARKER = '.reproduce-work'

NAMES = ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2', '2k+1']
TEXNAME = {'k^2+1': '$k^2+1$', 'k^3+2': '$k^3+2$', '2k+1': '$2k+1$', 't': '$t$ (formal)'}
POLY = {'k^2+1': (lambda k: k * k + 1, lambda k: 2 * k, 2),
        'k^3+2': (lambda k: k ** 3 + 2, lambda k: 3 * k * k, 3),
        '2k+1': (lambda k: 2 * k + 1, lambda k: 2, 1),
        't': (lambda k: k, lambda k: 1, 1)}
RATIOS = [.01, .02, .05, .1, .2, .4, .7, 1.]
PRIME_CUTOFFS = [10 ** 3, 10 ** 4, 10 ** 5, 10 ** 6, 10 ** 7]
# Rows of the exact-shape comparison (Table 5).  The linear polynomial has
# about x/2 moduli, so it is restricted to the two smallest sizes.
SHAPE_XS = {'k^2+1': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
            'k^3+2': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
            '2k+1': [250000, 1000000]}

mp.mp.dps = 80
I_CONST = -4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)          # I = -4 zeta(-1/2)
SIX_PI2 = 6 / mp.pi ** 2


def sha256(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def run_snapshot(work, reuse):
    accepted = json.loads(ACCEPTED.read_text())['artifacts']
    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
        if sha256(SNAP / name) != accepted[name]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'{name} does not match the accepted snapshot hash')
    elapsed = None
    if not (reuse and (work / 'results.json').exists()):
        if work.exists():
            # Only ever delete a directory that this script created itself.
            if any(work.iterdir()) and not (work / MARKER).exists():
                raise RuntimeError(f'{work} is not empty and was not created by reproduce.py; '
                                   'choose another --work directory')
            shutil.rmtree(work)
        work.mkdir(parents=True)
        (work / MARKER).write_text('scratch directory of manuscript/reproduce.py; safe to delete\n')
        for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
            shutil.copy2(SNAP / name, work / name)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(work / 'compute.py')], cwd=work, check=True)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
        if sha256(work / name) != accepted[name]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'work copy of {name} differs from the snapshot')
    results = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
    return results, elapsed


def all_rows(res, name):
    p = res['polynomials'][name]
    return p['rows'] + p['diagnostic_rows']


def compare_with_archive(new):
    old = json.loads((SNAP / 'results.json').read_text())
    out = {}
    for name in NAMES:
        o = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(old, name)}
        n = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(new, name)}
        if set(o) != set(n):
            raise RuntimeError(f'row sets differ for {name}')
        exact = all(o[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted'] == n[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted']
                    and o[k]['y'] == n[k]['y'] for k in o)
        dv = max(abs(Decimal(o[k]['V_decimal']) / Decimal(n[k]['V_decimal']) - 1) for k in o)
        po, pn = old['polynomials'][name], new['polynomials'][name]
        ce_o, ce_n = po['constant_extrapolated'], pn['constant_extrapolated']
        out[name] = dict(rows=len(o), integer_counts_identical=exact,
                         max_relative_difference_V=float(dv),
                         extrapolated_constant_difference=abs(ce_o['value'] - ce_n['value']),
                         envelope_difference=abs(ce_o['uncertainty'] - ce_n['uncertainty']),
                         fixed_ratio_slope_difference=abs(po['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']
                                                          - pn['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']))
    return out

# 2. Arithmetic helpers

def primes_upto(n):
    s = np.ones(n + 1, dtype=bool)
    s[:2] = False
    for p in range(2, math.isqrt(n) + 1):
        if s[p]:
            s[p * p::p] = False
    return np.nonzero(s)[0]


def powmod_vec(base, exp, mod):
    """Elementwise base**exp % mod for int64 arrays with mod < 3e9."""
    base = base % mod
    result = np.ones_like(mod)
    exp = exp.copy()
    while np.any(exp > 0):
        odd = (exp & 1) == 1
        result = np.where(odd, (result * base) % mod, result)
        base = (base * base) % mod
        exp >>= 1
    return result


def rho_formula(name, P):
    """(rho(p), rho(p^2)) for each prime in P, from the closed forms listed in
    Section 10.2.  They are checked against brute force by rho_bruteforce_check."""
    P = P.astype(np.int64)
    if name == 'k^2+1':
        r1 = np.where(P == 2, 1, np.where(P % 4 == 1, 2, 0))
        r2 = np.where(P == 2, 0, r1)
    elif name == 'k^3+2':
        cube = powmod_vec(np.full_like(P, -2), (P - 1) // 3, P) == 1
        r1 = np.where((P == 2) | (P == 3) | (P % 3 == 2), 1, np.where(cube, 3, 0))
        r2 = np.where((P == 2) | (P == 3), 0, r1)
    elif name == '2k+1':
        r1 = np.where(P == 2, 0, 1)
        r2 = r1.copy()
    elif name == 't':
        r1 = np.ones_like(P)
        r2 = np.ones_like(P)
    return r1.astype(np.float64), r2.astype(np.float64)


def rho_bruteforce_check(name, bound=1000):
    f = POLY[name][0]
    P = primes_upto(bound)
    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
    for i, p in enumerate(P):
        p = int(p)
        for m, expect in [(p, r1[i]), (p * p, r2[i])]:
            a = np.arange(m, dtype=np.int64)
            val = f(a) % m if name != 'k^3+2' else ((a * a % m) * a + 2) % m
            if int(np.count_nonzero(val == 0)) != int(expect):
                raise RuntimeError(f'rho mismatch for {name} at {m}')
    return len(P)


def local_factors(p):
    p = p.astype(np.float64)
    a_m1 = -3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3                                  # a_p - 1
    ba = -1 / p + p ** -1.5 + p ** -2 - p ** -2.5                     # b_p - a_p
    cb = -p ** -1.5 * (1 - p ** -0.5) * (1 - 1 / p)                  # c_p - b_p
    return a_m1, ba, cb


def euler_constant(name, P):
    """Partial values (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p and a rigorous interval for
    the full product (tail bound of Section 10.2)."""
    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
    xp, zp = r1 / P, r2 / (P.astype(np.float64) ** 2)
    a_m1, ba, cb = local_factors(P)
    s_m1 = a_m1 + ba * xp + cb * zp                                   # sigma_p - 1
    if np.any(1 + s_m1 <= 0):
        raise RuntimeError('nonpositive local factor')
    logs = np.log1p(s_m1)
    pref = 2 * float(I_CONST) / 3
    partial = {}
    for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS:
        partial[N] = pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N]))
    d = POLY[name][2]
    K = 3 + 2 * d
    N = PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]
    # |log prod_{p>N} sigma_p| <= K/(1-K/N^2) * sum_{p>N} p^-2, and every prime
    # p > N >= 30 lies in one of 8 classes mod 30, each contributing at most
    # N^-2 + 1/(30N).
    tail = K / (1 - K / N ** 2) * 8 * (1 / N ** 2 + 1 / (30 * N))
    val = partial[N]
    return dict(partial=partial, value=val, lower=val * math.exp(-tail),
                upper=val * math.exp(tail), tail_log_bound=tail, K=K)


def vaughan_c2(P):
    """c_2 = 8 C_1 (-zeta(-1/2)) / (3 zeta(2)^2), Vaughan (2005), (1.14)-(1.15)
    with k = 2; C_1 truncated to p <= N."""
    p = P.astype(np.float64)
    term = ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** 1.5 - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
    logs = np.log1p(term)
    pref = float(8 * (-mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / (3 * mp.zeta(2) ** 2))
    return {N: pref * math.exp(math.fsum(logs[P <= N])) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS}


def round_out(v, nd, up):
    """Round the float v to nd decimals, downwards (up=False) or upwards (up=True).
    Used for interval endpoints, so that the printed interval contains the
    computed one."""
    q = Decimal(1).scaleb(-nd)
    return Decimal(v).quantize(q, rounding=ROUND_CEILING if up else ROUND_FLOOR)


def certified_digits(lower, upper, maxdigits=12):
    """Longest decimal truncation shared by every number in [lower, upper]
    (0 < lower <= upper < 1); these digits are fixed by the interval."""
    best = None
    for nd in range(1, maxdigits + 1):
        a = round_out(lower, nd, False)
        b = round_out(upper, nd, False)
        if a != b:
            break
        best = a
    return str(best)


def euler_float_check(name, N=10 ** 5, dps=40):
    """Recompute (2/3) I prod_{p<=N} sigma_p with mpmath at dps digits, to
    gauge the floating-point rounding of euler_constant (not a certification)."""
    P = primes_upto(N)
    r1, r2 = rho_formula(name, P)
    with mp.workdps(dps):
        tot = mp.mpf(0)
        for p, a1, a2 in zip(P.tolist(), r1.tolist(), r2.tolist()):
            p = mp.mpf(p)
            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
            b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3
            c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
            xp, zp = mp.mpf(int(a1)) / p, mp.mpf(int(a2)) / p ** 2
            tot += mp.log(a * (1 - xp) + b * (xp - zp) + c * zp)
        return 2 * (-4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)) / 3 * mp.exp(tot)


def eligibility(results, name):
    """For the rows at the largest x: the largest delta for which the row lies in
    the range x^(7/9+delta) <= f(y) <= x^(1-delta) of Theorem 1.1(iii), computed
    from the actual ratio f(y)/x (negative: outside the range for every delta)."""
    rows = all_rows(results, name)
    xl = max(r['x'] for r in rows)
    out = []
    for r in sorted([r for r in rows if r['x'] == xl], key=lambda r: r['ratio_target']):
        lr = math.log(r['fy']) / math.log(xl)
        out.append(dict(x=xl, ratio_target=r['ratio_target'], ratio_actual=r['ratio_actual'],
                        delta_max=min(lr - 7 / 9, 1 - lr)))
    return out


def symbolic_local_identity():
    p = sympy.symbols('p', positive=True)
    r = sympy.sqrt(p)
    a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
    b = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + r) / p ** 3
    c = (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
    sig = a * (1 - 1 / p) + b * (1 / p - 1 / p ** 2) + c / p ** 2
    C1p = 1 + ((p - 1) ** 2 * p ** sympy.Rational(3, 2) - 2 * p ** 4 + 3 * p ** 3 - p) / (p ** 2 * (p ** 2 - 1) ** 2)
    checks = {
        'sigma_p(rho=1) == C_{1,p} (1-p^-2)^2': sympy.simplify(sig - C1p * (1 - p ** -2) ** 2) == 0,
        'a_p == (p-1)^2(p+2)/p^3': sympy.simplify(a - (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 2) / p ** 3) == 0,
        'b_p - a_p == -1/p + p^-3/2 + p^-2 - p^-5/2': sympy.simplify(b - a - (-1 / p + p ** sympy.Rational(-3, 2) + p ** -2 - p ** sympy.Rational(-5, 2))) == 0,
        'c_p - b_p == -p^-3/2 (1-p^-1/2)(1-p^-1)': sympy.simplify(c - b + p ** sympy.Rational(-3, 2) * (1 - 1 / r) * (1 - 1 / p)) == 0,
        'zeta(-1/2) == -zeta(3/2)/(4 pi)': abs(mp.zeta(-0.5) + mp.zeta(1.5) / (4 * mp.pi)) < mp.mpf(10) ** -70,
    }
    if not all(checks.values()):
        raise RuntimeError(f'symbolic check failed: {checks}')
    return {k: bool(v) for k, v in checks.items()}


def A0_mp():
    """A_0 = prod_p (1 - 2/p^2) to ~40 digits."""
    P0 = 1000
    small = [int(p) for p in primes_upto(P0)]
    head = mp.fsum(mp.log(1 - mp.mpf(2) / p ** 2) for p in small)
    tail = mp.mpf(0)
    for k in range(1, 30):
        pz = mp.primezeta(2 * k) - mp.fsum(mp.mpf(p) ** (-2 * k) for p in small)
        tail -= mp.mpf(2) ** k / k * pz
    return mp.exp(head + tail)


def Ah_mp():
    """A_h = prod_p (1 - 3/p^2 + 2/p^3) to ~40 digits."""
    P0 = 1000
    small = [int(p) for p in primes_upto(P0)]
    head = mp.fsum(mp.log(1 - mp.mpf(3) / p ** 2 + mp.mpf(2) / p ** 3) for p in small)
    tail = mp.mpf(0)
    for k in range(2, 30):
        ck = -(2 + mp.mpf(-2) ** k) / k
        pz = mp.primezeta(k) - mp.fsum(mp.mpf(p) ** (-k) for p in small)
        tail += ck * pz
    return mp.exp(head + tail)

# 3. MT(x; q) and h(q)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Arithmetic:
    """eta(t) for t <= tmax and the constants entering MT and h."""
    TSTAR = 64     # head of the eta-sums evaluated in 80-digit arithmetic

    def __init__(self, tmax):
        tmax = max(tmax, self.TSTAR + 1)
        self.tmax = tmax
        eta = np.ones(tmax + 1)
        eta[0] = 0.
        for p in primes_upto(tmax):
            p = int(p)
            eta[p::p] /= (p * p - 2)
            eta[p * p::p * p] = 0.
        self.eta = eta
        self.t = np.arange(tmax + 1, dtype=np.float64)
        self.kappa = eta * self.t ** 2
        self.eta_t2 = np.divide(eta, self.t ** 2, out=np.zeros_like(eta), where=self.t > 0)
        self.A0mp = A0_mp()
        self.A0 = float(self.A0mp)
        self.Ahmp = Ah_mp()
        self.head_cache = {}
        self.eta_mp = [mp.mpf(0)] + [mp.mpf(1) for _ in range(self.TSTAR)]
        for t in range(1, self.TSTAR + 1):
            fac = sympy.factorint(t)
            if any(e > 1 for e in fac.values()):
                self.eta_mp[t] = mp.mpf(0)
            else:
                self.eta_mp[t] = mp.fprod(mp.mpf(1) / (p * p - 2) for p in fac)

    def heads(self, qprimes, th):
        """80-digit A_0 * sum_{t<=th,(t,q)=1} eta(t) and eta(t)/t^2."""
        small = tuple(p for p in qprimes if p <= self.TSTAR)
        key = (small, th)
        if key not in self.head_cache:
            s2 = s4 = mp.mpf(0)
            for t in range(1, th + 1):
                if self.eta_mp[t] and all(t % p for p in small):
                    s2 += self.eta_mp[t]
                    s4 += self.eta_mp[t] / t ** 2
            self.head_cache[key] = (self.A0mp * s2, self.A0mp * s4)
        return self.head_cache[key]

    def MT(self, x, q, fac):
        """MT(x; q) for integer x, q with q <= x; fac = factorisation of q.

        Uses the factorisation t = t0 t1 t2 of the proof of Proposition 6.2:
        for t0 > sqrt(Z),
        B(Z/t0^2) = Z/t0^2 - Z^2/t0^4, and the complete eta-sums over t0 coprime
        to q are known in closed form, so the infinite t0-sum is evaluated
        exactly up to rounding."""
        S1 = [p for p, e in fac.items() if e == 1]
        S2 = [p for p, e in fac.items() if e >= 2]
        qprimes = list(fac)
        E2 = math.prod(1 + 1 / (p * p - 2) for p in S2)
        full2 = SIX_PI2 * mp.fprod(mp.mpf(p * p - 2) / (p * p - 1) for p in qprimes)
        full4 = SIX_PI2 ** 2 * mp.fprod(mp.mpf(p * p) * (p * p - 2) / (p * p - 1) ** 2 for p in qprimes)
        Tmax = math.isqrt(x // q)
        if Tmax > self.tmax:
            raise RuntimeError('tmax too small')
        ts = np.arange(1, Tmax + 1)
        cop = (self.eta[1:Tmax + 1] > 0) & (np.gcd(ts, q) == 1)
        total = 0.
        for r in range(len(S1) + 1):
            for sub in itertools.combinations(S1, r):
                t1 = math.prod(sub)
                eta1 = math.prod(1 / (p * p - 2) for p in sub)
                Z = x / (q * t1)
                T = math.isqrt(x // (q * t1))
                if T >= 1:
                    u = Z / self.t[1:T + 1] ** 2
                    fr = u - np.floor(u)
                    SB = float(np.sum((self.kappa[1:T + 1] * fr * (1 - fr))[cop[:T]]))
                else:
                    SB = 0.
                th = min(T, self.TSTAR)
                h2, h4 = self.heads(qprimes, th)
                br2, br4 = float(full2 - h2), float(full4 - h4)
                if T > self.TSTAR:
                    m = cop[self.TSTAR:T]
                    br2 -= self.A0 * float(np.sum(self.eta[self.TSTAR + 1:T + 1][m]))
                    br4 -= self.A0 * float(np.sum(self.eta_t2[self.TSTAR + 1:T + 1][m]))
                total += eta1 * t1 * (self.A0 * SB + Z * br2 - Z * Z * br4)
        return q * E2 * total

    def h(self, fac):
        """h(q) = I prod_{p not | q} a_p prod_{p||q} b_p prod_{p^2|q} c_p."""
        val = self.Ahmp * I_CONST
        for p, e in fac.items():
            p = mp.mpf(p)
            a = 1 - 3 / p ** 2 + 2 / p ** 3
            lam = (p - 1) * (p ** 2 - 2 + mp.sqrt(p)) / p ** 3 if e == 1 else (p - 1) ** 2 * (p + 1) / p ** 3
            val *= lam / a
        return float(val)


def factor_table(values):
    vmax = max(values)
    if vmax <= 2 * 10 ** 7:
        spf = np.zeros(vmax + 1, dtype=np.int32)
        for p in primes_upto(math.isqrt(vmax) + 1):
            p = int(p)
            blk = spf[p * p::p]
            blk[blk == 0] = p
        out = []
        for v in values:
            fac = {}
            while v > 1:
                p = int(spf[v]) or v
                while v % p == 0:
                    v //= p
                    fac[p] = fac.get(p, 0) + 1
            out.append(fac)
        return out
    return [{int(p): int(e) for p, e in sympy.factorint(v).items()} for v in values]


def identity_selftest(ar):
    """Check the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2) at x = 3000 for
    q <= 40, with every term computed by brute force except MT, which uses
    Arithmetic.MT.  Returns the largest relative discrepancy."""
    x = 3000
    sf = np.ones(x + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    sf[0] = 0
    for d in range(2, math.isqrt(x) + 1):
        sf[d * d::d * d] = 0
    c6 = float(SIX_PI2)
    Qx = int(sf.sum())
    worst = 0.
    for q in range(1, 41):
        fac = {int(p): int(e) for p, e in sympy.factorint(q).items()}
        g = np.empty(q)
        for l in range(q):
            v = c6 / q * math.prod(1 / (1 - p ** -2) for p in fac)
            for p, e in fac.items():
                if e == 1 and l % p == 0:
                    v *= 1 - 1 / p
                if e >= 2 and l % (p * p) == 0:
                    v = 0.
            g[l] = v
        n = np.arange(1, x + 1)
        counts = np.bincount(n % q, weights=sf[1:], minlength=q)
        E = counts - g * x
        V = float(np.sum(E ** 2))
        Dsum = 0.
        for hh in range(1, x // q + 1):
            m = hh * q
            C = int(np.sum(sf[1:x - m + 1] * sf[1 + m:x + 1]))
            A = ar.A0 * sum(ar.eta[t] for t in range(1, math.isqrt(m) + 1) if m % (t * t) == 0)
            Dsum += C - A * (x - m)
        rhs_wo_MT = 2 * Dsum + (Qx - c6 * x) - 2 * x * float(np.sum(g * E))
        mt = ar.MT(x, q, fac)
        worst = max(worst, abs(V - (mt + rhs_wo_MT)) / max(1., abs(V)))
    return worst


def shape_rows(results, ar):
    """For selected rows: V (snapshot), sum f'(k) MT(x;f(k)) and sum F(k) h(f(k))."""
    out = []
    for name in NAMES:
        f, fp, _ = POLY[name]
        rows = all_rows(results, name)
        for x in SHAPE_XS[name]:
            rr = sorted([r for r in rows if r['x'] == x], key=lambda r: r['y'])
            ymax = rr[-1]['y']
            qs = [f(k) for k in range(1, ymax + 1)]
            facs = factor_table(qs)
            mt = np.array([fp(k) * ar.MT(x, q, fa) for k, q, fa in zip(range(1, ymax + 1), qs, facs)])
            hf = np.array([fp(k) * math.sqrt(q) * ar.h(fa) for k, q, fa in zip(range(1, ymax + 1), qs, facs)])
            cmt, ch = np.cumsum(mt), np.cumsum(hf)
            for r in rr:
                y, Y = r['y'], r['fy']
                V = float(Decimal(r['V_decimal']))
                norm = math.sqrt(x) * Y ** 1.5
                out.append(dict(poly=name, x=x, ratio_target=r['ratio_target'], ratio_actual=r['ratio_actual'],
                                y=y, N_data=V / norm, N_MT=float(cmt[y - 1]) / norm,
                                V_over_sumMT=V / float(cmt[y - 1]), N_h=float(ch[y - 1]) / Y ** 1.5))
    return out

def fmt(v, nd):
    return f'{v:.{nd}f}'


def sci(x):
    e = int(round(math.log10(x)))
    m = x / 10 ** e
    if abs(m - round(m)) < 1e-9 and round(m) == 1:
        return f'$10^{{{e}}}$'
    mant = f'{x / 10 ** int(math.floor(math.log10(x))):g}'
    return f'${mant}\\cdot 10^{{{int(math.floor(math.log10(x)))}}}$'


def tex_sci(v):
    if v == 0:
        return '0'
    e = int(math.floor(math.log10(abs(v))))
    return f'{v / 10 ** e:.1f}\\cdot 10^{{{e}}}'


def write(path, text):
    path.write_text(text)
    return str(path.relative_to(HERE))


def make_outputs(results, compare, consts, c2, shape, selftest, symb, rho_checked, elapsed, floatcheck, elig):
    GEN.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    arts = []
    # Table: constants
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{l' + 'r' * len(PRIME_CUTOFFS) + 'l}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & ' + ' & '.join(f'$N=10^{{{int(math.log10(N))}}}$' for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS)
             + r' & interval for $C_f$ \\', r'\midrule']
    for name in NAMES + ['t']:
        c = consts[name]
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + ' & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(c['partial'][N], 9) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS)
                     + f" & $[{round_out(c['lower'], 9, False)},\\,{round_out(c['upper'], 9, True)}]$ \\\\")
    lines.append(r'Vaughan $c_2$ & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(c2[N], 9) for N in PRIME_CUTOFFS) + r' & \\')
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_constants.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: largest-x normalised values and stability
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{l' + 'r' * (len(RATIOS) + 1) + '}', r'\toprule',
             r'$r$ & $0.005$ & ' + ' & '.join(f'${r:g}$' for r in RATIOS) + r' \\', r'\midrule']
    for name in NAMES:
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        xs = sorted({r['x'] for r in p['rows']})
        xl = xs[-1]
        last = {r['ratio_target']: r for r in all_rows(results, name) if r['x'] == xl}
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + ' & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(last[r]['normalised'], 5) for r in [.005] + RATIOS) + r' \\')
        st = {s['ratio']: s['relative_change'] for s in p['stability']}
        dst = {s['ratio']: s['relative_change'] for s in p['diagnostic_stability']}
        ch = [dst.get(.005)] + [st[r] for r in RATIOS]
        lines.append(r'\quad change (\%) & ' + ' & '.join(f'${100 * c:+.4f}$' for c in ch) + r' \\')
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_largest.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: fits versus C_f
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & $\alpha+\beta$ (fixed $r$) & $\beta$ (fixed $x$) & $C_{\mathrm{extr}}\pm$ envelope & $C_f$ & $\frac{C_{\mathrm{extr}}-C_f}{C_f}$ & in envelopes \\',
             r'\midrule']
    fitsum = {}
    for name in NAMES:
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        fr, fx, ce = p['fit_fixed_ratio'], p['fit_fixed_x'], p['constant_extrapolated']
        Cf = consts[name]['value']
        rel = (ce['value'] - Cf) / Cf
        units = (ce['value'] - Cf) / ce['uncertainty']
        fitsum[name] = dict(alpha_plus_beta=fr['alpha_plus_beta'], alpha_plus_beta_se=fr['se'],
                            beta_fixed_x=fx['beta'], beta_se=fx['beta_se'], C_extrapolated=ce['value'],
                            envelope=ce['uncertainty'], C_f=Cf, relative_difference=rel,
                            difference_in_envelopes=units,
                            fit_coefficients=ce['primary_fit']['coefficients'],
                            cutoff_fits={str(v['ratio_cutoff']): v['value'] for v in ce['cutoff_fits']},
                            alternative_models={v['model']: v['value'] for v in ce['alternative_models']},
                            upper_window_fits={str(v['upper_ratio']): v['value'] for v in ce['upper_ratio_window_fits']},
                            previous_x_fit=ce['previous_x_fit']['value'],
                            joint_fit={k: p['fit_joint'][k] for k in ['alpha', 'alpha_se', 'beta', 'beta_se', 'C']})
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + f" & ${fr['alpha_plus_beta']:.4f}\\pm{fr['se']:.4f}$ & ${fx['beta']:.3f}\\pm{fx['beta_se']:.3f}$"
                     f" & ${ce['value']:.4f}\\pm{ce['uncertainty']:.4f}$ & ${Cf:.5f}$ & ${100 * rel:+.2f}\\%$ & ${units:+.2f}$ \\\\")
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_fits.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: model sensitivity of the extrapolation
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & primary & $C+a\sqrt r$ & $+\,r^{3/2}$ & $r\le 0.1$ & cutoff $0.005$ & previous $x$ \\', r'\midrule']
    for name in NAMES:
        fs = fitsum[name]
        lines.append(TEXNAME[name] + f" & {fs['C_extrapolated']:.5f} & {fs['alternative_models']['sqrt']:.5f}"
                     f" & {fs['alternative_models']['sqrt+linear+threehalves']:.5f} & {fs['upper_window_fits']['0.1']:.5f}"
                     f" & {fs['cutoff_fits']['0.005']:.5f} & {fs['previous_x_fit']:.5f} \\\\")
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_sensitivity.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Table: exact shape
    lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{llrrrrrr}', r'\toprule',
             r'$f$ & $x$ & $r$ & $y$ & $N_{\mathrm{data}}$ & $N_{\mathrm{MT}}$ & $V_f/\Sigma_{\mathrm{MT}}$ & $N_h$ \\', r'\midrule']
    prev = None
    for row in shape:
        if row['ratio_target'] not in (.005, .01, .1, 1.):
            continue
        key = (row['poly'], row['x'])
        if prev is not None and key[0] != prev[0]:
            lines.append(r'\midrule')
        lab = TEXNAME[row['poly']] if (prev is None or key[0] != prev[0]) else ''
        xl = sci(row['x']) if key != prev else ''
        prev = key
        lines.append(f"{lab} & {xl} & ${row['ratio_target']:g}$ & {row['y']} & {row['N_data']:.5f} & {row['N_MT']:.5f}"
                     f" & {row['V_over_sumMT']:.5f} & {row['N_h']:.5f} \\\\")
    lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'tab_shape.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Appendix tables: all normalised values
    for i, name in enumerate(NAMES):
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        xs = sorted({r['x'] for r in p['rows']})
        lines = [r'\begin{tabular}{l' + 'r' * len(RATIOS) + '}', r'\toprule',
                 r'$x$ & ' + ' & '.join(f'${r:g}$' for r in RATIOS) + r' \\', r'\midrule']
        for x in xs:
            vals = [next(r['normalised'] for r in p['rows'] if r['x'] == x and r['ratio_target'] == rt) for rt in RATIOS]
            lines.append(sci(x) + ' & ' + ' & '.join(fmt(v, 6) for v in vals) + r' \\')
        lines += [r'\bottomrule', r'\end{tabular}', '']
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'tab_full_{i}.tex', '\n'.join(lines)))

    # Plot data
    for i, name in enumerate(NAMES):
        p = results['polynomials'][name]
        xs = sorted({r['x'] for r in p['rows']})
        last = sorted([r for r in all_rows(results, name) if r['x'] == xs[-1]], key=lambda r: r['ratio_actual'])
        txt = 'r sqrtr N\n' + ''.join(f"{r['ratio_actual']:.10g} {math.sqrt(r['ratio_actual']):.10g} {r['normalised']:.10g}\n" for r in last)
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_ratio_{i}.dat', txt))
        C, a, b = fitsum[name]['fit_coefficients']
        grid = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
        txt = 'r sqrtr N\n' + ''.join(f'{r:.6g} {math.sqrt(r):.6g} {C + a * math.sqrt(r) + b * r:.10g}\n' for r in grid)
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_fit_{i}.dat', txt))
        txt = 'sqrtr N\n0 ' + f"{consts[name]['value']:.10g}\n"
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_cf_{i}.dat', txt))
        for rt, tag in [(.01, 'a'), (1., 'b')]:
            rr = sorted([r for r in p['rows'] if r['ratio_target'] == rt], key=lambda r: r['x'])
            txt = 'x N\n' + ''.join(f"{r['x']} {r['normalised']:.10g}\n" for r in rr)
            arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_x_{i}{tag}.dat', txt))
    for name in ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2']:
        i = NAMES.index(name)
        rr = sorted([s for s in shape if s['poly'] == name and s['x'] == SHAPE_XS[name][-1]], key=lambda s: s['ratio_actual'])
        txt = 'sqrtr Ndata NMT Nh\n' + ''.join(f"{math.sqrt(s['ratio_actual']):.8g} {s['N_data']:.10g} {s['N_MT']:.10g} {s['N_h']:.10g}\n" for s in rr)
        arts.append(write(GEN / f'fig_shape_{i}.dat', txt))

    # Numbers quoted in the prose of Section 10, with checks of the qualitative
    # statements made there (the script stops if one of them fails).
    xl = max(r['x'] for r in results['polynomials']['k^2+1']['rows'])
    lastrow = {name: {r['ratio_target']: r for r in all_rows(results, name) if r['x'] == xl} for name in NAMES}
    stab = {name: max(abs(s_['relative_change']) for s_ in results['polynomials'][name]['stability']) for name in NAMES}
    ndiag = [lastrow[n][.005]['normalised'] for n in NAMES]
    none_ = [lastrow[n][1.]['normalised'] for n in NAMES]
    betas = [fitsum[n]['beta_fixed_x'] for n in NAMES]
    sens_q = [fitsum['k^2+1'][k] for k in ['C_extrapolated', 'previous_x_fit']] + \
             [fitsum['k^2+1']['alternative_models'][k] for k in ['sqrt', 'sqrt+linear+threehalves']] + \
             [fitsum['k^2+1']['upper_window_fits']['0.1'], fitsum['k^2+1']['cutoff_fits']['0.005']]
    cutoffs = {results['polynomials'][n]['constant_extrapolated']['ratio_cutoff'] for n in NAMES}
    all_elig = [e for n in NAMES for e in elig[n]]
    best = max(all_elig, key=lambda e: e['delta_max'])
    claims = {
        'stability below 1% at every ratio': max(stab.values()) < 0.01,
        'k^2+1 and 2k+1 change much less than k^3+2': max(stab['k^2+1'], stab['2k+1']) < stab['k^3+2'] / 10,
        'one common stable cutoff': len(cutoffs) == 1,
        'extrapolations within their envelopes': all(abs(fitsum[n]['difference_in_envelopes']) <= 1 for n in NAMES),
        'k^2+1 sensitivity range brackets C_f': min(sens_q) < consts['k^2+1']['value'] < max(sens_q),
        'rows with r <= 0.01 outside the range for every delta': all(e['delta_max'] < 0 for e in all_elig if e['ratio_target'] <= .01),
        'C_t and Vaughan c_2 agree to 1e-8 at N=1e7': abs(consts['t']['value'] - c2[PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]]) < 1e-8,
    }
    if not all(claims.values()):
        raise RuntimeError(f'a statement of Section 10 is not supported by the data: {claims}')
    pct = lambda v: f'{100 * v:+.2f}'

    # Macros for numbers quoted in the text
    macros = {
        'CfQuadCert': certified_digits(consts['k^2+1']['lower'], consts['k^2+1']['upper']),
        'CfCubicCert': certified_digits(consts['k^3+2']['lower'], consts['k^3+2']['upper']),
        'CfLinCert': certified_digits(consts['2k+1']['lower'], consts['2k+1']['upper']),
        'CfTCert': certified_digits(consts['t']['lower'], consts['t']['upper']),
        'FloatCheck': tex_sci(max(floatcheck.values())),
        'StabCubic': f"{100 * stab['k^3+2']:.2f}",
        'StabOther': f"{100 * max(stab['k^2+1'], stab['2k+1']):.2f}",
        'NDiagMin': f'{min(ndiag):.3f}', 'NDiagMax': f'{max(ndiag):.3f}',
        'NOneMin': f'{min(none_):.3f}', 'NOneMax': f'{max(none_):.3f}',
        'BetaMin': f'{min(betas):.3f}', 'BetaMax': f'{max(betas):.3f}',
        'StableCutoff': f'{cutoffs.pop():g}',
        'RelQuad': pct(fitsum['k^2+1']['relative_difference']),
        'RelCubic': pct(fitsum['k^3+2']['relative_difference']),
        'RelLin': pct(fitsum['2k+1']['relative_difference']),
        'SensQuadMin': f'{min(sens_q):.3f}', 'SensQuadMax': f'{max(sens_q):.3f}',
        'XLargeInvCubeSmall': f'{xl ** (-1 / 3) * .01 ** -1.5:.1f}',
        'XLargeInvCubeOne': tex_sci(xl ** (-1 / 3)),
        'XTwoNinths': f'{xl ** (-2 / 9):.4f}',
        'DeltaRowOneMax': tex_sci(max(e['delta_max'] for e in all_elig if e['ratio_target'] == 1.)),
        'DeltaRowMax': f"{best['delta_max']:.3f}",
        'DeltaRowMaxR': f"{best['ratio_target']:g}",
        'CfQuad': f"{consts['k^2+1']['value']:.8f}", 'CfCubic': f"{consts['k^3+2']['value']:.8f}",
        'CfLin': f"{consts['2k+1']['value']:.8f}", 'CfT': f"{consts['t']['value']:.8f}",
        'VaughanCtwo': f"{c2[PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1]]:.8f}",
        'IConst': mp.nstr(I_CONST, 12),
        'ShapeMin': f"{min(s['V_over_sumMT'] for s in shape):.4f}",
        'ShapeMax': f"{max(s['V_over_sumMT'] for s in shape):.4f}",
        'ShapeRows': str(len(shape)),
        'ShapeDevLargest': tex_sci(max(abs(s['V_over_sumMT'] - 1) for s in shape if s['x'] == 256000000)),
        'SelfTest': tex_sci(selftest),
        'RerunMaxRelV': tex_sci(max(c['max_relative_difference_V'] for c in compare.values())),
        'RhoBound': str(1000),
    }
    tex = ''.join(f'\\newcommand{{\\{k}}}{{{v}}}\n' for k, v in macros.items())
    arts.append(write(GEN / 'macros.tex', tex))

    (GEN / 'snapshot_rerun_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1) + '\n')
    arts.append('generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json')

    repro = dict(
        description='All tables and plot data in the manuscript are generated by manuscript/reproduce.py; '
                    'see the per-artifact provenance below.',
        artifacts=arts,
        artifact_sources={
            'generated/tab_largest.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: results.json rows at the largest x, '
                                         'diagnostic ratio 0.005 rows, and stability (relative change between the two largest x).',
            'generated/tab_fits.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: fit_fixed_ratio, fit_fixed_x, constant_extrapolated; '
                                      'C_f from reproduce.py euler_constant (primes <= 1e7).',
            'generated/tab_sensitivity.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: constant_extrapolated alternative_models, '
                                             'upper_ratio_window_fits, cutoff_fits, previous_x_fit.',
            'generated/tab_constants.tex': 'reproduce.py euler_constant and vaughan_c2 (not part of the snapshot); '
                                           'partial products rounded to 9 decimals, interval endpoints rounded outwards.',
            'generated/tab_shape.tex': 'V from the snapshot re-run; sum f\'(k) MT(x;f(k)) and sum F(k) h(f(k)) '
                                       'from reproduce.py Arithmetic.MT / Arithmetic.h.',
            'generated/tab_full_*.tex': 'snapshot compute.py re-run: normalised values of all primary rows.',
            'generated/fig_ratio_*.dat, fig_x_*.dat': 'snapshot compute.py re-run rows.',
            'generated/fig_fit_*.dat': 'snapshot primary fit N(r)=C+a sqrt(r)+b r (coefficients from the re-run).',
            'generated/fig_cf_*.dat': 'reproduce.py euler_constant.',
            'generated/fig_shape_*.dat': 'as tab_shape.tex, at the largest x.',
            'generated/macros.tex': 'numbers quoted in the text, from the computations above (C_f digits fixed by the '
                                    'intervals, stability, fit and sensitivity ranges, eligibility of rows for Theorem 1.1(iii), '
                                    'self-test and shape statistics); see text_claim_checks.',
            'generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json': 'results.json written by the re-run of the snapshot compute.py (all rows and fits).',
        },
        snapshot_rerun=dict(seconds=elapsed, total_seconds_of_reproduce_py=None, comparison_with_archived_results=compare,
                            note='compute.py and counts.cpp copied unchanged (SHA-256 checked); counts.cpp compiled locally by compute.py.'),
        constants={name: dict(partial={str(N): v for N, v in c['partial'].items()}, value=c['value'],
                              interval=[c['lower'], c['upper']], tail_log_bound=c['tail_log_bound'], K=c['K'])
                   for name, c in consts.items()},
        vaughan_c2={str(N): v for N, v in c2.items()},
        I=mp.nstr(I_CONST, 20), A0=mp.nstr(A0_mp(), 25),
        constants_float_check=dict(note='relative difference between the double-precision partial product '
                                        'for p <= 1e5 and a 40-digit mpmath recomputation; not a certified bound',
                                   values=floatcheck),
        constants_certified_digits={n: certified_digits(consts[n]['lower'], consts[n]['upper']) for n in consts},
        eligibility_at_largest_x=elig,
        text_claim_checks=claims,
        rho_formulas_checked_by_brute_force_for_primes_below=1000, rho_primes_checked=rho_checked,
        symbolic_checks=symb,
        identity_selftest_max_relative_discrepancy=selftest,
        fits=fitsum,
        exact_shape_rows=shape,
        parameters=dict(prime_cutoffs=PRIME_CUTOFFS, shape_xs=SHAPE_XS, ratios=RATIOS,
                        MT_head_terms_in_80_digit_arithmetic=Arithmetic.TSTAR),
        caveats='Fitted constants and their envelopes come from the snapshot code; the envelopes are heuristic '
                'sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals. C_f intervals bound only the omitted primes; '
                'floating-point rounding is not included (see constants_float_check for an uncertified check).',
    )
    return repro


def write_reproduction(repro, total):
    repro['snapshot_rerun']['total_seconds_of_reproduce_py'] = total
    (HERE / 'reproduction.json').write_text(json.dumps(repro, indent=2) + '\n')


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--work', type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_WORK,
                    help='scratch directory for the snapshot re-run (default: scratch/reproduce-work)')
    ap.add_argument('--reuse-work', action='store_true',
                    help='reuse results.json already present in the work directory instead of re-running the snapshot')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    results, elapsed = run_snapshot(args.work.resolve(), args.reuse_work)
    print(f'snapshot results ready ({elapsed if elapsed is not None else "reused"})', flush=True)
    compare = compare_with_archive(results)
    print('comparison with archived results:', json.dumps(compare), flush=True)
    P = primes_upto(PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1])
    rho_checked = {name: rho_bruteforce_check(name) for name in NAMES + ['t']}
    consts = {name: euler_constant(name, P) for name in NAMES + ['t']}
    c2 = vaughan_c2(P)
    symb = symbolic_local_identity()
    xmax = max(max(v) for v in SHAPE_XS.values())
    ar = Arithmetic(math.isqrt(xmax) + 2)
    selftest = identity_selftest(ar)
    print(f'identity self-test: max relative discrepancy {selftest:.2e}', flush=True)
    if selftest > 1e-8:
        raise RuntimeError('identity self-test failed')
    shape = shape_rows(results, ar)
    floatcheck = {}
    for name in NAMES + ['t']:
        exact = euler_float_check(name)
        floatcheck[name] = float(abs(consts[name]['partial'][10 ** 5] / exact - 1))
    print('float check of the Euler products:', floatcheck, flush=True)
    elig = {name: eligibility(results, name) for name in NAMES}
    repro = make_outputs(results, compare, consts, c2, shape, selftest, symb, rho_checked, elapsed, floatcheck, elig)
    write_reproduction(repro, time.monotonic() - t0)
    print(f'done in {time.monotonic() - t0:.1f}s; wrote {HERE / "reproduction.json"}', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

                       SPARSE VARIANCE FOR PRIMES IN
                          ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION

                                J. BRÜDERN AND T. D. WOOLEY∗

        Abstract. An analogue of the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula is established
        for the variance of the number of primes in arithmetic progressions, in which the moduli
        are restricted to the values of a polynomial.




                                        1. Introduction
  The distribution of primes is a fundamental problem in the theory of numbers. Our
concern here is with the error terms that arise in the prime number theorem for arithmetic
progressions. Let 𝜙 denote Euler’s totient, and deﬁne the relevant quantity 𝐸(𝑥; 𝑘, 𝑙) for
real 𝑥 ≥ 2, and coprime natural numbers 𝑘 and 𝑙, through the equation

that was promptly reﬁned by Hooley [5], and now takes the shape
                    𝑉 (𝑥, 𝑦) = 𝑥𝑦 log 𝑦 + 𝑐𝑥𝑦 + 𝑂(𝑥1/2 𝑦 3/2 + 𝑥2 (log 𝑥)−𝐴 ).                     (1)
Here, the coeﬃcient 𝑐 is a certain real constant, the exponent 𝐴 is a preassigned positive
real number, and the relation (1) holds uniformly for 1 ≤ 𝑦 ≤ 𝑥. In this range, the

which is known as the Barban-Davenport-Halberstam theorem. If one singles out an
individual progression 𝑙 modulo 𝑘 from the mean 𝑉 (𝑥, 𝑦), then one recovers from the
bound (2) the Siegel-Walﬁsz theorem, the latter asserting that the estimate

\section{Provenance}\label{app:provenance}

The mathematics in \cref{sec:prelim,sec:densities,sec:identity,sec:pairs,sec:sawtooth,sec:single,sec:poly,sec:assembly} is an edited presentation of an archived run of a multi-agent proof pipeline in which language models proposed, proved and refereed the results. This appendix records where the material comes from. A proposition-by-proposition map, with every editorial change and correction, is in \texttt{manuscript/changes.md}.

\emph{Archive.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source repository: \url{https://gitlab.com/mshepherd/squarefree-numbers}, archive label \texttt{zt-neutral}.
\item Archive commit: \texttt{ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba}.
\item Harness commit: \texttt{33aadc609359221ba5d81664438bce5f658f561c}.
\item Revision recorded for all run stages: \texttt{8dfc53d01e56c9949c42061fdbe907a98a12a5d7}.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Models and roles (as recorded).} The model identifiers are those recorded in the archive. The command-line tool versions are not model-weight versions, and model versions beyond these identifiers are unknown.
\begin{itemize}[before=\raggedright]
\item Planning and probing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}; probing also \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5}.
\item Numerics: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} produced candidate computations. The \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} snapshot was accepted.
\item Proofs: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} (prover).
\item Refereeing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}. Each proposition was reviewed independently by both.
\item Integration (assembly audit): \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, independently.
\end{itemize}
Claude models ran under Claude Code 2.1.309 and Codex models under codex-cli 0.166.0. This write-up was produced by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} (Claude Code 2.1.311).

\emph{Workflow.} The problem statement restricts $f$ to $\Z[t]$. It asks for the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$ in as large a range of $f(y)\le x$ as can be justified, and it accepts a weaker range or error term provided it is correct. The weight $f'(k)$ and the class~\eqref{eq:f-hyp} of polynomials used here are those of the problem statement; neither was changed.
